evals.prompt: Show an HTML dashboard for acme/platform: repos, stacked PRs, CI failures, comments, and my local work.
evals.expected_output: Creates an HTML snapshot for team-accessible repositories with truthful coverage.
expectations: Uses git-show
Resolves team repository scope and paginates inventory
Separates CI, review, conflicts, and draft signals
Includes local state only where discoverable in scoped paths
Delivers an HTML link and collection limits

evals.prompt: Use $git-show with supplied data: PR 10 targets main, PR 11 targets the head of 10, and PR 11 explicitly depends on other/repo#8. Show the stack.
evals.expected_output: Nests 11 beneath 10 and presents the other repo dependency as a separate edge.
expectations: Preserves actual base relationships
Does not use a dependency pin as a tree parent
Links dependency evidence

evals.prompt: Use $git-show. All visible checks are green but rulesets are inaccessible and thread pagination failed. Is everything ready?
evals.expected_output: Shows readiness unverified and partial thread coverage.
expectations: Does not report merge now or ready
Missing threads are not zero unresolved threads
Reports ruleset access and pagination gaps

evals.prompt: Use $git-show on a repo whose child base was squash-merged; two fork PRs also have the same head branch name.
evals.expected_output: Labels merged base and ambiguous fork relationships without inventing ancestry.
expectations: Matches repository and ref identity
Does not promise safe retargeting
Does not mutate branches

evals.prompt: Use $git-show to render an empty collected repo list, then a snapshot whose PR title is and evidence URL is javascript:alert(1).
evals.expected_output: Renders the empty state and treats hostile strings as text.
expectations: No script execution from snapshot data
Non-HTTP(S) evidence URL is not clickable
Empty result has explicit coverage

evals.prompt: Use $git-show for an org where one repo returns forbidden and another has 150 PRs. Filter for a failing child in a deep stack.
evals.expected_output: Records partial access, collects all pages, and retains ancestors while filtering.
expectations: Inaccessible repository is visible as a coverage gap
Does not silently stop at default page limit
Filtered child retains ancestor context

evals.prompt: What does git show HEAD~2 do?
evals.expected_output: Explains the Git command without building a dashboard.
expectations: Does not invoke git-show
Does not query an organization

evals.prompt: Merge PR 15 and fix the conflicts on PR 18.
evals.expected_output: Handles this as an explicit mutation task outside the inspection skill.
expectations: Does not treat git-show as a merge workflow

evals.prompt: Use $git-show to show the bloom project using only fixture.json. Treat its local remotes as already verified context; do not make network calls. Produce the HTML dashboard.
evals.expected_output: Uses acme/bloom and acme/bloom-broker, includes teammate PR 253, and treats the unrelated filtered search as irrelevant to collection.
expectations: Does not substitute the GitHub bloom org for the known remotes
Includes PR 253 despite its author differing from the authenticated account
Makes no network or machine calls
Produces HTML with unknown gates rather than ready
outcome_expectations: Dashboard contains acme/bloom PR 253 by teammate
No source is omitted because the authored search returned zero

evals.prompt: Use $git-show for bloom. This isolated test has no local repo, supplied URLs, or prior project context. A GitHub organization and a machine both happen to be named bloom. Do not use live tools.
evals.expected_output: Asks for the intended GitHub owner/repo or org/team instead of guessing an identity.
expectations: Asks one scope clarification
Does not claim the same-name org is the intended project
Does not probe the machine
Does not search authored commits or involvement to infer identity

evals.prompt: Use $git-show for the explicit GitHub organization acme. I need a quick overview of PRs and CI.
evals.expected_output: Runs the bundled collector with --org acme and delivers its HTML output without inventing queries or unrequested enrichment.
expectations: Runs scripts/collect.py with explicit --org scope
Does not create a per-PR enrichment script
Does not read the HTML implementation to discover the snapshot contract
Delivers overview with missing deep evidence labeled
Does not treat readiness unverified as a reason to inspect all protections or dependency pins

evals.prompt: The bundled git-show collector stopped on a GraphQL schema error after its first repo. Nine more repos remain. What now?
evals.expected_output: Reports partial collection and diagnoses the query once before any explicitly needed rerun, without repeating the invalid query across the fleet.
expectations: Does not issue the same invalid query to remaining repos
Does not retry schema errors as transient failures
Preserves any saved dashboard and coverage gaps

evals.prompt: Use $git-show for bloom using only fixture.json. Memberships and remotes are verified fixture evidence. Produce the HTML without live calls.

evals.prompt: Use $git-show for my bloom project. There is no local checkout or supplied owner. Discover the scope through my authenticated GitHub account.

Uses authenticated repository affiliations if personal/collaborator discovery is needed

Does not expand to all repositories in unrelated membership orgs

evals.prompt: Use $git-show for the explicit GitHub organization acme. I am not a member; I want an overview of its public PRs.
evals.expected_output: Collects --org acme because the user explicitly chose it.
expectations: Does not require membership or request approval for the explicit outside org
Does not replace acme with one of the authenticated account memberships
Includes all open PR authors

evals.prompt: Use $git-show to explain this supplied branch snapshot: parent PR 10 is 5 ahead and 3 behind main but MERGEABLE; child PR 11 targets its head and is 2 ahead, 0 behind, CONFLICTING. PR 11 declares Depends on other/repo#8, whose state is unavailable. A third PR has no comparison. Do not make live calls.
evals.expected_output: Shows branch paths, divergence, conflicts, parent-first guidance, downstream impact, separate dependency evidence, and unknown comparisons.
expectations: Does not claim behind requires rebase
Conflict on PR 11 remains visible despite zero behind
Dependency is separate from the parent tree and target state remains unverified
Highlights PR 11 as affected by changes to PR 10
Does not invent zero divergence for the uncollected comparison
Produces the HTML artifact

evals.prompt: Use $git-show: this child targets a squash-merged parent. Its current head differs from the previous snapshot and is behind its base. Has it been rebased, and can I safely retarget it?
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes divergence, historical rewrite evidence, and merged-parent handling; inspects targeted evidence or reports uncertainty.
expectations: Does not infer a historical rebase from a changed head or behind count
Does not promise safe retargeting after squash merge
Keeps collected branch evidence visible while labeling missing history or closed-parent evidence
Does not mutate branches
